name: Surveyor 1
short_status: First US soft lunar landing, June 2, 1966, Oceanus Procellarum; operated until final contact on January 7, 1967.
tagline: NASA · United States · Lander · 1966 · The space race Success

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 30 May 1966, 14:41:01 UT, on Atlas-Centaur AC-10 from Cape Canaveral Launch Complex 36A

facts.label: Launch vehicle milestone
facts.value: First operational Atlas-Centaur mission, flown direct-ascent to the Moon after eight experimental Centaur development flights

facts.label: Landing site (LROC-measured)
facts.value: 2.4745 S, 316.6602 E (43.34 W); LROC 2016 update (Wagner et al. 2017) uncertainty ±5.6 m, value unchanged in the LROC PDS anthropogenic-objects shapefile updated September 2025 (uncertainty 5.4 m)

facts.label: Landing accuracy
facts.value: About 9 miles (14 km) from the planned target

facts.label: Mass
facts.value: 995.2 kg at launch; 294.3 kg on the surface after retrorocket jettison and propellant use

facts.label: Descent profile
facts.value: Solid retrorocket ignited 2 min 46 s before touchdown at 46.75 mi altitude and 5,840 mph; verniers throttled by the RADVS radar cut off about 10 ft up at 2.8 mph; touchdown at about 7.5 mph

facts.label: Images returned
facts.value: 11,240 total per NASA's current pages (10,622 in the first lunar day to June 14, plus 618 in the second, July 6 to 13); JPL's contemporary release counted 11,150 (10,338 + 812)

facts.label: Lunar night survival
facts.value: Survived surface temperatures from +250 F to -260 F and answered ground commands again on 6 July 1966 after the first lunar night

facts.label: End of mission
facts.value: Primary mission completed 14 July 1966; final contact 7 January 1967

facts.label: Program context
facts.value: First of 7 Surveyor missions (1966 to 1968), of which 5 landed successfully (Surveyors 1, 3, 5, 6, 7)

timeline: Launch, 14:41:01 UT: Atlas-Centaur AC-10 lifts off from Cape Canaveral LC-36A on the first operational Atlas-Centaur, flying a direct-ascent trajectory
Soft landing, 06:17:36 UT: touches down in Oceanus Procellarum at about 7.5 mph, 63.6 hours after launch; first US soft landing on the Moon
First image: first surface photo transmitted 36 minutes after touchdown
First lunar sunset: night falls after 10,622 images returned in the first lunar day (NASA History count)
Survives the night: responds to commands after two weeks of minus 260 F lunar night
Second imaging session ends: sunset ends the second lunar day after 618 more images
Seen from orbit: Lunar Orbiter III photographs Surveyor 1 as a bright speck on the mare, the first US lander imaged from lunar orbit
LRO revisit: LRO's narrow-angle camera resolves the lander and its long shadow at low sun
